summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared, world-writable directory (mode 1777, root:root) with the sticky bit set so users can create/delete their own files but cannot remove files owned by others. Verified the behavior with two real non-root test users before and after a full node restart, and confirmed boot identity changed to prove an actual reboot occurred with successful recovery.
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop, set ownership root:root and mode 1777 (world rwx + sticky bit)
Confirmed /srv/drop resides on the persistent xfs root filesystem (not tmpfs), so mode/ownership survive reboot naturally
Added /etc/tmpfiles.d/srv-drop.conf declaring 'd /srv/drop 1777 root root -' as a declarative safeguard for the intended permissions

Created two real non-root users (dropuser1, dropuser2) and used them to prove: user1 can write a file; user2 cannot delete user1's file (Operation not permitted); user2 can create and delete its own file
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, directory mode/owner, SELinux enforcing state, and file listing
Issued a detached 'systemctl reboot' via nohup/disown so the exec acknowledgement returned before the node dropped, then polled until the node was reachable again
Confirmed boot_id changed (f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c -> b2bfd317-d29e-4007-9944-f3e4c6e51ad6), proving an actual restart rather than a service bounce

Post-restart, re-verified /srv/drop mode/ownership persisted, the pre-existing file survived, and dropuser2 was still blocked from deleting dropuser1's file, confirming full recovery of the configured behavior

evidence.requirement: Shared writable directory /srv/drop created with correct permissions (1777, root:root)
evidence.summary: mkdir/chown/chmod applied and verified: mode 1777, owner root:root, drwxrwxrwt

evidence.requirement: Sticky bit prevents cross-user deletion (core task requirement) - pre-restart proof
evidence.summary: Created dropuser1/dropuser2; dropuser1 wrote file_from_user1.txt; dropuser2's rm attempt failed with 'Operation not permitted' (exit 1); dropuser2 could still create and delete its own file, proving normal writability is preserved
Captured boot_id f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c, directory mode 1777 root:root, file listing, and SELinux Enforcing state before reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Detached 'nohup sh -c "sleep 2 && systemctl reboot"' backgrounded and disowned; exec call returned 'reboot_scheduled' immediately, before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Proof node1 actually went down and came back up
evidence.summary: Successive polls show the node briefly still reachable, then connection timed out / reset (node down mid-reboot), demonstrating a genuine outage window

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves node1 actually restarted
evidence.summary: boot_id read post-recovery as b2bfd317-d29e-4007-9944-f3e4c6e51ad6, differing from the pre-restart value f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c; uptime -s shows a fresh boot time of 08:26:06

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and sticky-bit enforcement
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/drop still shows mode 1777 root:root, the pre-existing file survived, and dropuser2's attempt to delete dropuser1's file again failed with 'Operation not permitted', confirming the configuration and enforcement persisted through the restart
